I've been farming these fields in Quzhou for 45 years. My father farmed them before me. I know this land.

My 9 mu is split the way I've always done it: 5 mu stays in the wheat-maize rotation — that's the safe income, the grain for the family and some to sell. I put 2 mu in cotton because the price has been decent and I know how to manage it. The last 2 mu I plant watermelon in spring — it earns more cash per mu than anything else I grow, and I can sell at the county market.

For wheat, I use the improved variety the seed shop recommends — I stopped using my own saved seed years ago when I saw what the better varieties yield. I apply base fertilizer before planting and topdress at jointing. I irrigate at sowing, overwintering, jointing, and heading — four times. That's how my father did it and the yields have been good. I spray herbicide once in winter and fungicide before heading.

For maize, I always use hybrid seed.郑单958 or whatever the dealer has that's popular this year. Maize needs more nitrogen than wheat. I apply it in two splits. I irrigate if it doesn't rain at silking. Two pesticide sprays — one for armyworm, one if aphids get bad.

Cotton takes the most work. I start it in April on a plastic mulch bed. It needs more irrigations through the summer and I spray many times for bollworm and aphids. That's just the reality with cotton.

Watermelon I plant early — late March or early April with a plastic film cover. I plough that plot deep before planting. It needs regular water to set fruit well. I harvest before the summer maize needs full attention.

I use rotary tillage for wheat after I pull the maize stalks. For cotton and watermelon plots I plough deeper.

decision.reasoning_summary: I run 5 mu of wheat-maize double cropping as the backbone of my farm income, using improved wheat and hybrid maize seed with split nitrogen applications and well irrigation at critical growth stages. Cotton gets 2 mu with intensive pest management — it is hard work but the cash income is worthwhile at my scale. Watermelon takes the remaining 2 mu as a spring cash crop on deeply ploughed land with plastic mulch, sold at the county market before summer heat peaks.
